title: Reset failure
summary: A failed reset receipt names its failure: a check row's name and ok come from the operation, never nested evidence. When the server refuses a receipt, test_machine_operation_submit_failed repeats the host's error code, reason and recovery. A failed macOS reset keeps its first error code, and failed_calls records each failed call's exit code and bounded stderr, or its exception type and message; the runner's own SSH failure (exit 124) is test_mac_reset_transport_failed. Sign-in refusals (test_machine_sign_in_newer_than_baseline, test_machine_sign_in_app_quit_not_proved, test_machine_sign_in_app_probe_failed when pgrep fails rather than finds no Safari) stop before anything is cleared, as do the Terminal refusals: test_machine_terminal_quit_not_proved when Terminal survives its quit and a forced kill of its window processes, and test_machine_terminal_probe_failed when pgrep fails. After a successful restore the reset relaunches Terminal without saved windows; test_machine_terminal_relaunch_failed means no window appeared. A harness probe whose reply the parser rejected keeps a sanitized reply_rejection record (rejection branch, event types, final event shape, exact-OK/tool-use/degraded-context booleans, harness exit code; never reply text) on its failed row; a QA run stores it as a probe_reply_rejection artifact and names the branch in its verdict reason. A golden sealed before these records returns none and its reason asks for a recapture.
